Record date: 2129-07-24
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/24/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath, persistent cough, and continued lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up after a week on the revised treatment regimen initiated during his last visit. He reports that while the oral antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate) were initiated as planned, he has experienced only minimal improvement in his respiratory symptoms. The patient continues to experience significant shortness of breath, particularly during activities of daily living, and describes his cough as persistent with occasional greenish-yellow sputum production. He denies any fever or chills but notes increased fatigue and a sense of overall malaise.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant issue, with persistent discomfort and limited mobility. He reports adherence to the furosemide regimen but states that the edema has not improved substantially, and he continues to experience pitting edema upon examination. The patient has also been practicing the cognitive-behavioral techniques for insomnia, but he feels that his sleep quality remains poor.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent shortness of breath, + cough with greenish-yellow sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg - Heart Rate: 90 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 24 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 87% on room air
General: The patient appears in moderate respiratory distress, with increased work of breathing noted.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with wheezing; bilateral crackles are more pronounced in the lower lung fields compared to the previous visit.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, with significant pitting noted, particularly in the calves.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with inadequate response to current treatment; concern for possible pneumonia given the change in sputum color and increased respiratory distress. 2. Congestive heart failure with persistent fluid overload; furosemide regimen appears insufficient at current dosing. 3. Insomnia, with ongoing cognitive-behavioral strategies in place but requiring further evaluation.
PLAN
1. Order a chest X-ray to evaluate for possible pneumonia or other pulmonary complications, given the patient's change in sputum color and worsening respiratory status. 2. Initiate a course of oral prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days to reduce airway inflammation and improve respiratory symptoms. 3. Increase furosemide to 160 mg daily to enhance diuresis and address persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every 2 hours and nebulized budesonide every 6 hours. 5. Monitor potassium levels closely due to the increased furosemide and initiate spironolactone at 25 mg daily to assist with fluid retention. 6. Reassess insomnia management; consider a trial of low-dose trazodone if cognitive-behavioral strategies continue to be ineffective. 7. Educate the patient on the importance of adhering to the new medication regimen and recognizing signs of worsening infection or heart failure.
The patient demonstrated understanding of the updated treatment plan and expressed willingness to adhere to the new regimen.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge, with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 07/31/29. He was instructed to seek immediate care should he experience any acute changes in his condition, including increased shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant weight gain.
